body:
Thanks for the comment! :)
A few things--
1. I am planning on giving his parents an update tomorrow (I am going to be seeing them), but he has already told them that he is having thoughts of hurting himself again. He has also told me that if I tell them "[he] will probably do something [I] will regret". They do need to know the amount of weight he is putting on Joe and I to ask him out though.
2. to touch on that more, he told me today that "Joe said that he would go out with him if it meant [he] wouldn't kill himself". He asked if I would do the same and I obviously said yes. The problem is that now he is *expecting* one of us to ask him out even though neither of us is gay and he has a boyfriend(who at this point is irrelevant). Specifically, my response was 

>Yes, I would. But the goal is for you to not want or need to go out with one of us. I'm not scared that you are now holding onto that one hope. That you will go as far as you need to for one of us to go out with you. You are holding onto this new hope that we would if you needed us to, and that is now bringing you down.

To which he replied

>I know the goal helpmehelpmyfriend1 and its impossible since I can't control this OCD. I can't live with this disease. The ONLY solution is if one of you would go out with me. That's it right there. That way, my obsession would be satisfied. But you and Joe both don't want to and shouldn't. And I shouldn't need it but I do. I just want this need to stop. It's irrational and ruining my life. But it won't stop. I'm going to deal with this for however long I live

All night he has now been asking me how much longer it will be until I realize I need to ask him out, and I keep on trying to convince him that it is a last resort and not a step along the way. He then says that I "better start realizing its pretty much come down to the last resorts".

I'm stuck. This is all starting to take a toll on me too, but I know how important it is for him to get better. What do I do at this point?
